newsitem.title: CONGO: Japanese nationals leave Zaire's capital.
newsitem.headline: Japanese nationals leave Zaire's capital.

text.p: Ten Japanese nationals, mostly businessmen, left Zaire's capital Kinshasa for neighbouring Congo at the weekend, fearing a deterioration in the security situation there, Western diplomats said on Monday.
The 10 planned to leave Congo's capital Brazzaville, a ferry ride across the Zaire River from Kinshasa, for home shortly, the diplomats added. The 10 arrived in Brazzaville on Sunday.
More than 1,000 U.S., French, Belgian and British troops are in Congo or off its coast on stand-by in case they need to evacuate their nationals from Zaire's volatile capital.
Rebels vowing to topple veteran president Mobutu Sese Seko now control half of Zaire, including the diamond, copper, cobalt and gold mines of its economic heartland.
